Spoke with Rob regarding the situation where an application was completed, marked as delivered, and used to obtain funding so parts could be ordered before the repairs were completed. He explained that this involved a specific customer who wanted to secure approval but keep the vehicle until the required parts arrived. Because he could not release the vehicle without ordering the parts, he marked the deal as delivered to receive funding.

I reminded Rob that this is not the correct process. The proper procedure is to obtain approval, complete all repairs on the vehicle, and only then mark the application as delivered once the work has been completed. Applications should not be marked as delivered at any point prior to the completion of repairs. Rob acknowledged the issue and stated that he will not do this again moving forward.

Subject: 00UTO00000csAEH2A2
Full Comments:
I spoke with Stephen, the owner. He said business continues to be steady, and EasyPay is currently the only financing option they offer, so we don’t have any competition in the shop. Because the surrounding area has a mix of income levels, they see a fairly even split between approvals and declines.

The main challenge is that when Stephen isn’t at the shop, EasyPay typically isn’t offered. The front desk employee is older and has repeatedly said she doesn’t want to learn the system, telling me she “doesn’t mess with that stuff.” I’ve offered to train her several times, but she has declined each time. This likely limits the number of applications they could be submitting, although Stephen is in the shop most of the time, so the impact is somewhat limited.

I left him some swag and reminded him to reach out to Connor or me if he ever needs anything.

Full Comments:
Checked in via Maps Application 
Spoke with Lalo, the shop owner. He said business has been extremely slow. He explained that many businesses throughout the Valley are struggling due to increased ICE activity in the area, rising parts costs, and higher vehicle repair prices. As a result, many customers are either postponing repairs or only paying for the bare minimum needed to keep their vehicles running. Lalo mentioned that this is the slowest summer he’s experienced in the five years he’s been in business. He’s hopeful that business will begin to improve in August and September.
